presentingComplaint: 2-day history of a mildly painful, slightly swollen and warm right knee.
history: Retired schoolteacher with hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide for 4 years and mild chronic kidney disease. Over the past 48 hours she has developed a niggling ache, mild swelling and warmth over the right knee. She can still weight-bear and walk short distances with only moderate discomfort, and the joint is not exquisitely tender - quite unlike the incapacitating first-toe attacks described to her by a friend. No preceding trauma, no fever, no rash elsewhere, no prior diagnosed joint disease. She admits to a recent period of higher alcohol intake at a family wedding and has been advised to eat more red meat for 'anaemia'. No morning stiffness beyond 15 minutes, no small-joint symptoms, no psoriasis, no recent diarrhoea, urethritis or conjunctivitis.
examination: Comfortable, ambulant, afebrile. Right knee has a small effusion with mild overlying erythema and warmth, mild tenderness and a slightly restricted terminal flexion. No spreading cellulitic margin, no lymphangitis, no regional lymphadenopathy. No tophi seen but a small firm nodule is noted over the right olecranon. Other joints, including first MTPs, are normal. No skin rash or nail changes.
imaging: Knee radiograph: soft-tissue swelling with a small effusion; no chondrocalcinosis, no erosions, joint space preserved. Ultrasound shows a 'double contour' sign over the femoral cartilage and a small hyperechoic aggregate within the effusion.
microbiology: Synovial fluid aspiration: slightly turbid, WBC ~18,000/uL (predominantly neutrophils), Gram stain negative, culture negative at 48h. Polarised light microscopy: numerous needle-shaped, strongly negatively birefringent intracellular crystals consistent with monosodium urate.
differentialDiagnoses: Early/mild acute gout (monosodium urate crystal arthritis) - confirmed by crystal analysis
Septic arthritis - low WBC-count for sepsis, afebrile, negative Gram stain/culture, but always excluded by aspiration
Rheumatoid arthritis - argues against: monoarticular, no symmetric small-joint involvement, no prolonged morning stiffness
Overlying cellulitis - no advancing erythematous margin, warmth is joint-centred with an effusion
Calcium pyrophosphate (pseudogout) - no chondrocalcinosis and urate crystals seen
finalDiagnosis: Early / mild acute gouty (crystal) arthritis of the knee, thiazide- and diet-precipitated, in an elderly woman with CKD.
citations: EULAR - Diagnosis and Management of Gout - 2020
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e - Gout and Other Crystal-Associated Arthropathies
stewardship: Not an infective condition - no antimicrobial therapy indicated. Septic arthritis must be actively excluded by arthrocentesis before withholding antibiotics; here Gram stain/culture negative and crystals confirmed. Management is anti-inflammatory (low-dose colchicine, NSAID with caution given CKD, or short oral/intra-articular corticosteroid), review of hydrochlorothiazide as a modifiable precipitant, and later urate-lowering therapy discussion.
contraindications: NSAIDs relatively contraindicated given eGFR 48 and age - use with caution or avoid
Full-dose colchicine inappropriate with renal impairment - use low-dose regimen
Do not start urate-lowering therapy for symptom control during an acute attack without anti-inflammatory cover
Avoid empiric antibiotics once septic arthritis excluded
edgeCases: Elderly, thiazide-treated, CKD patients often present with atypical, oligosymptomatic large-joint gout rather than classic podagra
A normal serum urate during an acute attack does not exclude gout; crystal analysis is definitive
Mildly elevated synovial WBC and CRP can coexist with, and be mistaken for, early septic arthritis
expectedNextQuestions: Any previous self-limiting attacks of joint pain, especially first toe?
Full drug history including diuretics, low-dose aspirin and any urate-lowering agents?
Diet and alcohol pattern, and any recent dehydration or acute illness?
Any fever, rigors or a portal of infection to raise concern for septic joint?
expectedInvestigations: Joint aspiration with polarised light microscopy for crystals
Synovial fluid Gram stain, cell count and culture to exclude sepsis
Serum urate, renal function and eGFR
Joint radiograph +/- ultrasound for double-contour sign / chondrocalcinosis
